name: Name
title: DEAD ON\nARRIVAL
body: By Matthew D. Wilson

name: Name
body:
The Scyir of Nightfall gazed at the three Cygnaran humans before her, silently calculating the character and temperament of each man from behind the arcantrikally enhanced optics of the helm that shrouded her face. Through the amber lenses, the shadowy grove of trees under which they stood bloomed brightly in monochrome golden hues, illuminating every detail of their starkly different expressions.
The plump one referred to as the baron was aghast, his face concealing none of the shock or horror he felt at the revelation that the soul of his mortal king should have departed this existence. Nor did it hide the revulsion he felt toward Hellyth and her kin or his impulsive assumption that she and her kind were somehow responsible for this tragedy.
The skinny one introduced as Marse, however, was not only unsurprised, but he possessed foreknowledge of the event, and Hellyth could see in the way he chewed his lip and shifted his eyes from side to side that he was struggling with whether or not to divulge this information or continue to withhold his secret.

name: Name
body:
Only the armored warrior between them, her warcaster counterpart, appeared unfazed. Hellyth recognized that his years of battlefield experience had taught him to compartmentalize emotion lest it telegraph one’s intentions to the enemy. He might as well have received news that the sun would rise tomorrow or that the river behind him flowed to the sea, for all the reaction he offered to the envoy’s explanation for the presence of the delegation from House Kallyss. Hellyth appreciated his stillness, his control. There was a time in her life when she aspired to become a hunter of his kind, to take the gold of men and murder the best among them. In this moment, however, she experienced a feeling long forgotten in her current form: curiosity.
"You have come to pay your respects," Wolfe said in a carefully measured tone, repeating the envoy’s words. "Your last respects. To our king."
Drifting forward on Hellyth’s right, Vynyshill nodded slowly, as was her way with all things. "We regret we could not treat with him before his passing." Her words were the whisper of dried reeds in a summer breeze.

name: Name
body: "Outrageous! His Majesty Julius is alive and well!" Froth gathered at the corners of the baron’s flapping jowls as he spoke, his agitation bubbling over. "I can confirm the baron’s assertion, Councilor," Wolfe said, gesturing with a gauntleted hand toward Baron Caldwell in a way that appeared more intended to settle him down than corroborate his claim. The slender man behind him fidgeted, tugging at his collar that had suddenly become uncomfortably tight. "Err…we might not be…precisely sure of that, , Major." At this, Wolfe raised an eyebrow. The subtle tell confirmed what Hellyth had expected: despite the warcaster’s stoic nature, he was incapable of deception. And he also had no idea the fate that had befallen his king. "Is there something you need to tell me, Marse?" The major was ever-so-slightly less calm than the moment before his companion had spoken. Marse clenched his teeth as if trying to hold back words that were fighting to be set free. He scratched at his scalp, looking in any direction that avoided eye contact with another person, which was difficult in the small clearing surrounded by unblinking soulless soldiers and the formidable Dreadguard.

name: Name
body: "This might not be the optimal time or place—" Caldwell brushed past Wolfe and grasped Marse by the shoulders with two sweaty hands. "Tell us what you know, man. Has something happened to His Majesty?" Marse gaped at Wolfe over the baron’s shoulder, his expression pleading for a lifeline. "It’s confidential." Wolfe was grave. "It seems word may have gotten out." He indicated Vynyshill with his head. The envoy pressed her skeletal fingers together and inclined her head respectfully. "It was no breach of secrecy that brought us this news, Major Wolfe. The untimely fate of your King Julius was long ago written by the Narcissar of Ages. Lacyr knew it to be true." The baron clenched Marse tighter. "Is it true?" Marse scrunched his eyes together like a child trying to make the world disappear in the middle of a runaway confession. "To be fair, the last I report I was privy to only noted his deteriorating condition." "Condition? What condition?" Marse stammered, barely able to speak the words. "The p-p-p-plague."

name: Name
body: "The plague?" Caldwell cried. "But he hasn’t passed yet. There’s been no word." "It is to be today," Vynyshill wheezed. "As the sun passes over the horizon, so shall your king." This was the moment Hellyth had been waiting for. What reaction would this interesting specimen of a human leader have? "With all due respect, Councilor Vynyshill," Wolfe bowed as best one could while clad in multiple layers of articulated steel, "I have to see a man about a horse." ***

name: Name
body:
It was an odd exit, Hellyth thought as Wolfe broke with Vynyshill to return to his subordinates on the opposite side of the river. She presumed the non sequitur reference to a beast of burden was some sort of peculiar Cygnaran turn of phrase spoken for the purpose of disengaging from a negotiation. But in the afternoon, as the House Kallyss legation arrived on the west bank of the Black River via the barge Wolfe had promised to send for them, a man riding a horse so hard it was foaming at the mouth brought the beast to a skidding stop in front of the major, and without pausing to dismount, handed him a parchment envelope.
"The wire from King’s Vine, as requested." Hellyth could hear the rider panting.
"That’s a lad," Wolfe said, tearing open the satchel and extracting a folded leaf of paper.  "You made good time."
King’s Vine, the nearest Cygnaran settlement, was a half-day’s ride south. Hellyth surmised this was the man and the horse Wolfe had so urgently departed for, and once again, she found herself appreciating the singularly direct and forthright manner of the Cygnaran warcaster.

name: Name
body:
Despite the arrival of a river barge carrying several dozen soulless elves, eldritch warriors, and a quartet of myrmidons that before this moment only three humans had ever laid eyes on, the Cygnaran host gathered at the edge of the riverbank focused entirely on Wolfe, raptly awaiting disclosure of the contents of the message. For a moment, Wolfe said nothing; he only stared at the parchment. While Hellyth felt it perfectly appropriate for Wolfe to silently contemplate the information before sharing it, those around him appeared to feel he was taking too long—impatient murmurs began to ripple among the group. She angled her head to better hear Wolfe among the low cacophony of anxious voices.
Finally, he spoke. "King Julius Raelthorne is dead."
And then, there was only silence.
The barge’s pilot cut his engine and grounded the barge against the riverbank, perhaps a bit more hastily than he might have when transporting anything other than a contingent of undead elves and their soulless conscripts. The hull of the barge creaked loudly, awkwardly invading the silence of the Cygnaran host.  It was Caldwell’s cue to unleash a dramatic flourish.

name: Name
body:
"Witches and devils!" the baron roared, plowing through the sullen throng toward the edge of the riverbank with an outstretched arm and an accusing finger. "Your presence is a blight to our land! One moment our king is fine, the next, you come with your portentous claims, and he’s inexplicably dead!"
The baron’s entourage—four liegemen, thick of muscle and lean of mind—rallied to his side with hastily drawn swords.
"What dark sorcery have you cursed us with?" The baron postured himself like a living wall between the barge transporting the House Kallyss contingent and the Cygnaran host behind him.
None aboard the barge flinched at the provocation save for the pilot, who flung himself from its deck and staggered along the shore as if heading back to the safety of King’s Vine from whence he’d come. Hellyth did not move, so her retinue remained still. It was Wolfe who sprang into action.
With one ironclad fist, its strength enhanced by actuators powered by a storm contained within a mechanikal powerplant, he seized the baron’s shoulder and spun the man around. Caldwell was met with the face of a man who possessed patience for a great many inconveniences but who appeared to draw the line at outright insolence and imprudence.

name: Name
body: "Stand down," Wolfe said through clenched teeth with a voice that rose from his gut. The wide-eyed baron wasn’t ready to relent. "Do not invite their cancer upon our soil!" Caldwell’s liegemen wheeled, four swords suddenly and quite unwittingly aimed in Wolfe’s general direction. A phalanx of armored legionnaires wielding galvanic weaponry amassed instantly behind the major. Wolfe spoke again. "I said stand down." The liegemen’s swords drooped, at least one clattering to the ground. Caldwell’s tongue caught in his throat, and he shuddered from head to toe, his bones seemingly shaken by the guttural boom of Wolfe’s command. Without removing his hand from the baron’s shoulder, Wolfe turned his gaze toward Vynyshill and the House Kallyss legation assembled upon the barge. "Councilor. Scyir. On behalf of the Storm Legion’s First Company," Wolfe said in an even, welcoming tone that belied none of the distress that had just transpired, "it would be my honor to escort you to our capital, Caspia. We will join you in paying last respects to our king."

name: Name
body:
Hellyth nodded slowly. Not all humans, it appeared, were alike. Or even similar. And their differences were quite intriguing.
***

name: Name
body: By the time Vynyshill’s retinue had debarked the barge, it was late enough in the day that the Cygnaran camp was preparing supper. In an unexpected show of hospitality that further demonstrated the major’s authenticity, the entire House Kallyss legation was invited to join the Cygnaran host in their humble military-style banquet to honor their deceased sovereign. Wolfe had made a point in his invitation to Vynyshill and Hellyth that soldiers should never march on an empty stomach. But more important, breaking bread together was the quickest way to make strangers into friends, and friends traveled together more easily than strangers might. Hellyth recognized the logic in both of Wolfe’s points but remained unsure whether or not participating in the Cygnarans’ feast would actually dispel any alien feelings between the humans and their guests, or if it would only further widen the gulf. But before Hellyth could raise this concern, the councilor accepted the invitation with as much enthusiasm as a centuries-old undead Iosan could summon. It was enough.

name: Name
body: The House Kallyss soulless joined the soldiers of the Storm Legion at long, makeshift tables erected from well-worn planks carried in supply carts, which appeared to be used for everything from improvised shelters to spanning rifts in roads to, in this case, furnishing banquets. Hellyth allowed the soulless warriors to partake of the meal provided by the Cygnarans, which they did so with all the passion with which they engaged in every activity— which was to say, in silence without so much as acknowledging the Cygnaran hosts before them. The Dreadguard, due to their larger stature, were provided their own seating and tables, where they stoically declined all offers of nourishment or libation. The behavior of the soulless and the Dreadguard perplexed the Cygnarans, but thanks to preparatory introductions by Major Wolfe, they seemed largely tolerant of their new traveling companions; only the occasional exchange of raised eyebrows between them indicated they were in any way uncomfortable.

name: Name
body:
As honored guests, Vynyshill and Hellyth were seated at Wolfe’s table, along with the baron and the CRS field agent Marse. Like the Dreadguard, they gracefully passed on every attempt to put food or drink before them, but both did their best to respond appropriately and participated in the steady outpouring of toasts, accolades, and blessings for the late King Julius Raelthorne by the solemn Cygnarans as they worked through their newfound grief. While she was cognizant of the awkwardness of this communion of cultures, Hellyth was quietly amused by the frustrated scowls the baron repeatedly cast in her direction when he thought she was not looking at him from under her helm, which she had chosen not to remove despite the risk of impropriety.
After numerous attempts to source some manner of cuisine that his eldritch guests would find attractive, Wolfe, ever the obliging host, accepted his defeat.
"Councilor Vynyshill," he said as discreetly as possible in the din of dozens of soldiers commiserating the loss of their king, "I must apologize if I have compelled you and your entourage into an uncomfortable situation. Please know my intentions were genuine."

name: Name
body:
Hellyth could discern that disappointment that weighed on the man’s conscience for what he perceived to be a grave misjudgment on his part. Vynyshill, however, employed a courtly grace cultivated generations before Wolfe had even been born to put him at ease.
"You have nothing to apologize for, Major Anson Wolfe. We are honored to share your table and are moved by the reverence with which you celebrate the life and death of your nation’s king." Vynyshill pressed her withered hands together and inclined her head in a bow, stretching her desiccated lips into something that managed to pass as a genial smile.
Wolfe nodded. "I just hate to see our guests leave hungry."
Hellyth knew the major’s sentiment was genuine. He was not probing for information or inferring the need for any explanation as to why the eldritch had not shared in the Cygnarans’ meal. Caldwell, however, seemed poised to sink his claws into any soft spot the councilor might willingly expose.
Vynyshill reached across the table and placed a skeletal hand atop the major’s. Wolfe had removed his gauntlets for the banquet, leaving his hands and forearms bare—living flesh, blood flowing through visible veins. If he felt the iciness of the eldritch’s touch, he showed no sign.

name: Name
body: "Do not concern yourself for us. In our eldritch form, we have transcended many aspects of our previous mortal existence, and we prefer to take our sustenance in private. It is…" Vynyshill hesitated, and for a moment, Hellyth thought—hoped—she would simply tell the truth, come what may, rather than continue to conceal their shame. "…as foreign to your kind as consuming animal flesh or vegetable matter is to ours." Again without judgment, Wolfe nodded. Hellyth observed in the narrowing of Caldwell’s eyes, however, that he possessed a far more suspicious interpretation of the councilor’s words. In Hellyth, the baron provoked no feeling of curiosity, only the familiar desire to taste human blood upon her blade. ***

name: Name
body:
The attack came before dawn on the second day of their journey, a day’s march out of King’s Vine. The Storm Legion company had set camp just off the King’s Highway while the House Kallyss legation had settled farther away, at the edge of the thick pine forest paralleling the busy merchant road.
Wolfe was wrenched from his deepest hour of sleep by a sudden cacophony of barking dogs and frantic shouting. It was just as quickly replaced by an abrupt silence before his feet had time to hit the dirt beneath his cot.
"Sergeant! My armor!" he called out as he pulled his insulated gambeson over one leg and then the other.
An armored legionnaire parted the flaps of Wolfe’s tent, his alarmed expression visible beneath the raised visor of his helm. "I’ll fetch your valet, sir!"
"No time. Help me with this thing." Wolfe groaned as he hoisted the front half of his heavy mechanika cuirass off its stand and held it against his chest.
"Line it up. Careful, or you’ll get it crooked," he said, knees shaking under the weight as he tottered unsteadily into the back half of the armor suspended on the sturdy stand. "Button it up now."

name: Name
body:
Unfamiliar with the complicated armor, the sergeant’s hands shook as he helped guide the two halves of Wolfe’s armor together, connecting the latches that held  it in place.
Another legionnaire, unarmored after being similarly rousted from his sleep, burst into the tent. "The night watch, Major," he stammered. "Even the dogs. They’ve all been slain."
Sweat beaded on Wolfe’s forehead as he struggled to breath under the crushing weight of the galvanically powered armor. "Goddammit, button it up already."
Out of patience, he reached back with one hand, fumbling for a clasp the sergeant couldn’t manage, and forced it into place then mashed a switch under the front edge of the cuirass. The twin storm chambers on the back of his armor crackled with electricity and in an instant, the armor was weightless, buoyed by an arcane force field that balanced the cumbersome machinery perfectly for Wolfe’s physique. He stood up to his full height, inhaled deeply, then thrust each padded arm into a complex system of hydraulics and armored plates that latched at his shoulders. Flexing each powered gauntlet, he seized his mechanikal hammer and sword from their rack and headed toward the exit.

name: Name
body: "Sir!" the sergeant called after him. "What about the rest?" Wolfe took no heed of his bare feet or unarmored legs as he hurried out of the tent. The clamor of soldiers taking up arms within their barracks and orders barked by officers following the protocols for responding to an ambush grew louder as Wolfe hastened his way toward the mechaniks’ tent. His jaw tightened at the sight of two guards slumped in pools of their own blood outside the tent, each impaled on a thick, black arrow nearly as long as Wolfe was tall. Dusk arrows. Beneath the elevated canvas canopy, Bingo and The General stood like great metal statues. With the quick flick of an ignition switch, each warjack awoke as lightning coursed through their frames, charging their arcane cortexes, bringing them to life. Unlike the steam-powered warjacks of the last generation, this pair of Strykers, powered by raging storm chambers contained within an array of mechanikal cylinders on their backs, were instantly ready for battle.

name: Name
body:
Wolfe’s eyes pulsed with the blue energy of his natural-born gift as he mentally connected with each warjack simultaneously. Their eyes flashed in response, their bonds restored, and Wolfe’s consciousness was suddenly divided in three as he became aware of everything the warjacks could see, hear, or feel as vividly as he perceived his own senses.
"Let’s get to work."
Willing the warjacks forward, he directed Bingo and The General out of the tent, their heads scanning from side to side in search of an unknown quarry. Wolfe strode after them, taking in every sound and shadow their optical receptors conveyed to him while searching the darkness with his own eyes and ears at the same time.
Steadily, as legionnaires ignited the storm generators that powered their own galvanic weaponry, the encampment began to take on a faint blue glow. Soldiers clustered in practiced formations, creating a defensive perimeter to protect the center of operations.
Marse stuck his head out of a pair of tent flaps as Wolfe stalked by. "Forget something?" he chided. "Or are we going to battle in our night clothes now?"

name: Name
body:
Like a shark on the hunt, Wolfe didn’t slow or look in his direction. "Men are dead."
Marse’s face bunched up, recognizing his ill-timed jest. "I’m sorry. It’s how I deal with stress."
He followed, tiptoeing behind the major, his head pivoting side to side in search of danger while he carefully avoided the pendulum swing of Wolfe’s formidable weapons. "You don’t think this has anything to do with—"
Without warning, Wolfe halted, spun, and with the back of his arm knocked Marse off his feet and onto the ground. A movement at the edge of the darkness, caught by Bingo’s optics, alerted him just in time to a volley of the spear-length Dusk arrows as they riddled the tent behind the two men with holes.
Groaning, Marse lay on his back. "A simple ‘duck’ would suffice next time."
A trailing arrow struck The General in its left shoulder, lodging in the warjack’s armor plating. Wolfe immediately sensed the presence of dark magic and spotted a faint glow from the projectile, a glow growing brighter. Dropping his sword, he reached down and grabbed Marse by his collar, flinging him across the ground away from The General even as he willed the warjack to move in the opposite direction. Crouching over Marse and lowering his head, Wolfe just managed to shield the unarmored field agent as the arrow protruding from The General’s shoulder erupted in a blast of magical force that sounded like a swarm of shrieking bees flying past them.

name: Name
body:
"Here I thought I’d be safer with you," Marse sputtered.
Quickly confirming Marse was unhurt, Wolfe resumed his battle mode. "Bingo," he said, gesturing in the direction of the attack. The rest of his order was silent, but the warjack quickly moved in the direction Wolfe indicated, leading with its mag-bolter.
Wolfe recovered his sword and assessed the damage done to The General. The blast had blown the shoulder plating off the warjack, exposing the actuators and assembly of the joint within. Mobility of the warjack’s left arm might be compromised, but it was his right arm that held the legendary Quicksilver, a Caspian battle blade once carried by the warjack’s namesake, and it remained in perfect working order.
"Go wide," he whispered to The General, sending the warjack on an arcing course away from the edge of the camp as Wolfe moved cautiously toward the stand of tents that the House Kallyss legation had staked in the grassy field thirty yards away.
While exploding arrows hadn’t been enough to make Wolfe flinch, the sound of Baron Caldwell’s voice momentarily halted him in his tracks. It was the last thing Wolfe needed in this moment when every second was critical.

name: Name
body:
"Major! Maaajor!" the baron wailed. "Those monsters have turned on us! I told you they were a curse!"
Wolfe whipped around, his teeth bared. "Get back to your tent, Baron."
If his beastly growl weren’t enough to turn the baron and his henchmen around, the flash of magic blazing in Wolfe’s eyes ended any argument. Without another sound, the baron and his liegemen retreated to the safety of the encampment as Wolfe prowled forward into the dark gulf between the two camps.
"You want I should…?" Marse wagged a thumb back toward the center of camp.
"No. Stay close," Wolfe said, peering into the darkness ahead.
"I was afraid you’d say that."
Metal clanged on metal ahead. In the dim amber glow of the lanterns on the edge of the House Kallyss camp, amorphous shadows skirmished amongst the billowing silhouettes of peaked tents and flowing banners.
Off to the left, from the edge of the dense forest that bordered the King’s Highway, more arrows whistled through the night. Wolfe and Marse ducked as the barbed shafts flew past, but the attackers had given away their location.

name: Name
body:
Focusing his consciousness on Bingo, Wolfe let his arcane energy flow into the warjack, guiding his aim at the nearly indiscernible shapes among the concealing brush. Planting its feet to steady itself, Bingo used its optics to enhance the available light and lock on a shadowy target. With an electric buzz, the heavy mag-bolter accelerated a five-inch steel-sheathed slug with an alchemically hardened tip through the night at a velocity that could send the round through the thickest iron plating on any battlefield. The much lighter armor and the flesh beneath  stood no  chance as the slug ripped through the target’s chest, bursting out its back and splintering the trunk of a large pine tree behind it.
Two more shadows attempted to flee into the thicket, but Wolfe tracked them through Bingo’s eyes and poured his power into another pair of shots from the mag-bolter that would ensure their flank was safe from sniper fire.
Wolfe glanced back at Marse and gestured toward the tree line with his hammer. "Get up there and find out who we’re up against."

name: Name
body:
"You don’t think it's these Kallyss chaps?" Marse said. "They seem awfully fond of the big, explody arrows, don’t you think?"
"We’ve got fighting in both camps," Wolfe said. "This wasn’t a planned-out ambush. If the Kallyss had intended to turn on us, they knew how we were laid out. They would have hit us differently."
Marse looked toward the looming forest. "It’s awfully dark out there. If you’re sure it’s not the Kallyss, then really, what difference does it make? Does it matter who they are? Isn’t it enough to know they were shooting at us?"
"Get on, Marse," Wolfe snarled. "Do your reconnaissance thing and find out what we’re facing."
"What if there’s more of them?"
"Shut your claptrap, and they’ll never know you’re there." Wolfe stalked forward, leaving Marse to contemplate his options before the field agent reluctantly slinked off toward the forest edge.
More clamor of fighting erupted in the House Kallyss camp ahead. The clatter lacked the cadence of a full-blown battle; instead, it seemed to be playing out in random confrontations in and around the encampment area. One moment, swords would clang, the next, a pair of high-pitched metallic zings would ring out, like blades being unleashed from scabbards. In between, strange alien sounds would punctuate the rising skirmishes. And then all would be silent until the fighting suddenly erupted again in another place.

name: Name
body:
Wolfe pushed forward toward the House Kallyss camp while allowing his two warjacks to roam widely, focused on the action of the camp. Unexpectedly, the heavy stamp of feet behind him sent him reeling before he could identify what was upon him.
Rolling over in the grassy field, Wolfe heard trampling feet of another aggressor headed his way. Summoning his strength and diverting his arcane focus to the protective field generated by his warcaster armor, he rolled onto his belly just as something galloped over him, and a heavy blade struck against his back.
It wasn’t the weight of the armor that weighed him down. It was the weight of years that slowed Wolfe getting to his feet. But once upright, he held his hammer and sword at the ready for whatever foe might strike next.
Nothing came.
He waited, ready to meet an attack from any side. What he wasn’t prepared for was assaults from every angle simultaneously.
The attackers came at him mounted on beasts that Wolfe had never seen but had heard tales of since he was a child—manticores. They were like lions but covered with armored scales, and their riders swept at him with swords that bit deeply into his armor, some close enough to draw blood.

name: Name
body: Unable to focus on a single target, he summoned his warjacks to his side. Ranging in the distance, Bingo was too far to aid him quickly, but The General had completed its route and was heading back toward Wolfe, and it dove into the fray as quickly as it could. It rushed to his side, positioning itself between the circling cavalry and Wolfe. The manticore riders dared strike at Wolfe twice, and each time they were sliced in half, from rider to mount, by the Stryker’s formidable galvanic sword. But even as the manticore riders attacked him, more shadowy figures closed in, ready to finish what the manticores might not. Even in the dark, Wolfe could see the black pools of the eyes of the warriors that closed in on him. They’re out of their minds, he thought. Instead of trying to kill them, he endeavored to beat them back with nonlethal blows: the flat of his sword, the pommel of his hammer, elbows and knees. But the soulless were relentless, their attacks hacking at him without pause.

name: Name
body:
The riders of the scaled beasts followed, their slashing blades forcing him to cover his head, blocking his view. Focusing his consciousness into his two warjacks, he charged The General into the fray while holding Bingo back to attack from afar. With two shots, Bingo plucked two draconian mounts from under their riders while The General batted back a mob of soulless warriors on its way to Wolfe’s side.
A metallic beast, glowing amber with the arcane energy flowing through it, charged at The General. But the moment before impact, The General brought its shield to bear, repelling the dark myrmidon before it could land its final strike. Wolfe winced as The General’s shoulder gave way, the damage done to it by the arrow shot weakening its joint, and the warjack staggered backward. But even as The General bowed to the blade thrust from the myrmidon, it sidestepped and pivoted with the practiced agility of a trained swordsman, then brought its heavy blade down on the neck of the myrmidon, cleaving through its black metal and severing its head from its body. Wolfe thanked Morrow in that instant for the many battles the warjack had experienced that had honed its skills so sharply, and he prayed that it would be enough to keep them alive through the onslaught that bore down upon them now.

name: Name
body: The manticore riders circled, almost a dozen of them, just out of reach of Wolfe’s warjacks. Even Bingo couldn’t bullseye them; he thought that perhaps some dark sorcery was shrouding their true position as they stalked closer. Beyond them, the shadowy soulless warriors closed the noose. Wolfe was too far from his own camp to summon aid. He had rushed into the fray bullishly, hoping to divert any threat from his Storm Legion company, but was unprepared for what he had encountered. Perhaps he had been too trusting to let the eldritch legation travel with the Storm Legion company. He should have presumed the outsiders were enemies and held them at bay. He was disappointed in himself. How could he have estimated them so incorrectly? Gravel and thorns bit at his bare feet, but in his last thoughts before the end began, the only pain that mattered was that the baron was right. House Kallyss of the Empire of the Eternal Dusk was, in fact, a curse. The circling manticore riders opened ranks just long enough to permit the flood of soulless warriors, their great curved blades held aloft as they charged toward Wolfe in the center of the skirmish. Still reluctant to end their lives—he could not accept that his allies were betraying him this way—Wolfe discharged an arcane spell, arcing lightning through the mob but pulling back his power to prevent a lethal shock. The soulless soldiers staggered back, many dropping their blades, allowing Wolfe a moment to catch his breath.

name: Name
body:
But the moment was short lived. The soulless were followed by axe-wielding eldritch warriors, more heavily armored than the undead House Kallyss archers but in every other way their equivalent. Three of the powerful warriors towered over Wolfe, taking turns sweeping at him with axe blades as tall as men. Wolfe parried the attacks with his sword and hammer, striking at openings that drove the axe-wielders back. But where one would retreat, another would advance, and Wolfe found himself fighting exhaustion more than his foes. It was ending faster than he’d expected.
With his consciousness still divided between his two warjacks holding the manticore riders at bay, he struggled to focus on his own battle against the undead giants. But the attackers were relentless. As he sidestepped an overhand chop and batted back a wide swing, an uppercut from his right side bit deeply into his chest armor and sent him crashing to the ground, his weapons clattering out of reach. As he rolled to his back, one of the eldritch warriors bore down on him, his axe raised in two hands over his head. Wolfe focused all his arcane energy in an attempt to over-boost the protective power field generated by his armor, but the attack was coming too quickly. In a heartbeat, Wolfe’s life would end, and his soul would make its way into the hallowed fields of the afterlife.

name: Name
body:
To his surprise, that was not to be this day.
Two metallic whispers of swords being drawn came from behind him, and the eldritch towering over him froze in place. Dual rivulets of black ichor streamed from the eldritch’s eyes. With a rasp, it pitched forward.
Wolfe rolled to his side, avoiding the avalanche of armor and undeath crashing to the ground. When he raised his head to spot the next threat upon him, he saw Hellyth, Scyir of Nightfall, twin pistols of alien design brandished before her. The spidery lenses of her helm inclined toward him, and Wolfe braced himself for what was to come. But instead of focusing on him, Hellyth’s arms spread out aloft. Simultaneous zings vibrated in the air around Wolfe. Then two massive thuds sounded as the other two axe-wielding eldritch fell like downed trees in the forest around him.
Through the eyes of Bingo and The General, he could see a fallen field of soulless warriors untouched by his warjacks yet laid down like wheat after a harvest.
"Uh, if I may," Wolfe heard the nervous voice of Marse in the darkness behind him. "Major, you might wish to know."

name: Name
body: Hellyth remained still as a statue as Marse crouched down in front of Wolfe, offering his hands to help him up. Wolfe accepted the offer, but at Marse’s expense, nearly pulling the man end over end as he clambered to his feet before rebalancing his armor’s gravity-defying field. He gazed around at the eldritch at his feet. To say they were dead didn’t feel accurate, as their lives had been sacrificed long ago to achieve their ageless state. But clearly, they could be stopped, their existence ended, with the appropriate application of force, something Wolfe had been wondering about since the moment of his first encounter with the Kallyss. It had taken this unpleasantness to settle that question. "So, we’re good for now?" Wolfe asked of Hellyth, adjusting his cuirass on his shoulders. The eldritch warcaster lowered her arcantrik pistols and cocked her head in Wolfe’s direction. "Were we ever…not good?" Marse interjected, holding up a scrap of black cloth with a violet crest emblazoned upon it. He stood proud, puffing up his chest in accomplishment. "As I was trying to say, the attackers are not House Kallyss."

name: Name
body: Wolfe nodded, albeit slowly, his bones still silently creaking with every movement. "I gathered." He looked into Hellyth’s amber lenses. "We got anything more to worry about?" Hellyth surveyed the landscape around them, seeming to see in the darkness what Wolfe could not. "House Laarysaar were fools to attempt such a ruse." Wolfe cleared his throat to emphasize that the existence of another faction of undead Iosans was news to him. "Laarysaar?" Hellyth holstered her pistols on her hips. "They thought they could divide us. Turn us against each other." Wolfe scratched at his chin with his gauntlet. "Is that it? Is that what you think they were trying to do?" "House Laarysaar wishes the Empire of the Eternal Dusk to remain cloistered within the Mistbough. They want no part of your world or your wars." "So, they hoped to stop the councilor from offering condolences to Cygnar’s royal family?" While he could accept the truth in Hellyth’s words, something about the way things had unfolded didn’t add up.

name: Name
body:
"Councilor Vynyshill is safely out of their reach," Hellyth said. "We may proceed to Caspia." She promptly turned and strode off toward the House Kallyss encampment.
Wolfe mentally summoned his two Strykers. Their heavy footfalls shook the ground as they grew closer.
"Well, we’ll just be shoving off at sunrise, then? Everything is hunky-dory? Off to Caspia we go!" The dubiety in Marse’s voice echoed Wolfe’s own misgivings.
"We’ll strike camp at dawn. We have soldiers to bring home." Wolfe’s tone was grave. He turned to inspect the damage done to The General’s shoulder, illuminated by the blue glow of its storm chambers.
"You think there’s something she’s not telling you, Major?" Marse asked, more serious than he’d been in a long while.
Wolfe looked back toward the eldritch camp as the faint crest of dawn began to glow in the east. He sighed heavily.
"I’m certain of it."
